fact_text: NCCPL settles a sale of shares bought on an earlier trading day on a first-in, first-out basis, so the oldest purchase lots are treated as sold first.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'FIFO & LIFO in PSX Trading | NCCPL Settlement Explained' (YouTube, 2026-08-06)

fact_text: Shares bought and sold on the same trading day are settled on a last-in, first-out basis, so the most recent purchase lot is matched against the sale first.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'FIFO & LIFO in PSX Trading | NCCPL Settlement Explained' (YouTube, 2026-08-06)

fact_text: Three lots of 100 shares bought at Rs 10, Rs 12 and Rs 14 make 300 shares with a total cost of Rs 3,600 and an average buying price of Rs 12.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'FIFO & LIFO in PSX Trading | NCCPL Settlement Explained' (YouTube, 2026-08-06)

fact_text: In the worked example, selling 150 of the 300 shares at Rs 16 under FIFO gives a realised profit of Rs 800, from 100 shares at Rs 10 and 50 shares at Rs 12 as cost.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'FIFO & LIFO in PSX Trading | NCCPL Settlement Explained' (YouTube, 2026-08-06)

fact_text: After the FIFO sale in the worked example, the 150 shares left (50 at Rs 12 and 100 at Rs 14) have an average buying price of about Rs 13.33.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'FIFO & LIFO in PSX Trading | NCCPL Settlement Explained' (YouTube, 2026-08-06)

fact_text: In the intraday example, 100 shares bought at Rs 14 and 50 shares from the Rs 10 lot are sold at Rs 16 under LIFO, giving a realised profit of Rs 500 on Rs 2,400 of sales.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'FIFO & LIFO in PSX Trading | NCCPL Settlement Explained' (YouTube, 2026-08-06)

fact_text: After the intraday sale in the example, the 150 shares left (50 at Rs 10 and 100 at Rs 12) have an average buying price of about Rs 11.33.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'FIFO & LIFO in PSX Trading | NCCPL Settlement Explained' (YouTube, 2026-08-06)

fact_text: If shares are bought again after a sale on the same trading day, the sale is matched to that later purchase under LIFO, so a Rs 12 sale of a Rs 13 purchase shows a Rs 1 loss, even though the system may show a profit.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'FIFO & LIFO in PSX Trading | NCCPL Settlement Explained' (YouTube, 2026-08-06)

fact_text: The analyst's view was that an investor booking profit on a trading day should avoid a later purchase that would be matched against the sale, or buy only at lower prices, so the booked profit is not turned into a loss.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'FIFO & LIFO in PSX Trading | NCCPL Settlement Explained' (YouTube, 2026-08-06)
